meta.title: Hindi A2 Elementary
meta.subtitle: 750 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Hindi → English (see the Hindi, recall the meaning) and English → Hindi (see an English meaning, recall the Hindi). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 750 words for an elementary learner, aligned to A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand sentences and frequently used expressions related to areas of most immediate relevance' — a learner here is able to manage simple, routine exchanges of information on familiar matters — personal and family information, shopping, the local area, work — and to describe in simple terms their background, their surroundings and what they immediately need. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Hindi, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 241 of the 750 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — relatives and the people around you, work and study, jobs, clothes and shopping, more food and cooking, the furniture of a home, the town, the countryside and animals, the seasons and the points of the compass, the months, the numbers to a crore, travel, health and the body, feelings and character, free time and festivals, telling what happened and when, giving an opinion, and the everyday verbs of moving, dressing and doing — and the other 509 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Hindi, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every form of a noun or a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword is printed in Devanagari with a romanisation beneath it, Wiktionary's own (ā ī ū for the long vowels, a tilde or a dot for nasalisation: khānā, ma͠i), so the deck can be studied before the script is fluent; the Hindi Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script itself. The 493 nouns show their gender, masculine or feminine, which every adjective, postposition and past-tense verb agrees with, and their plural; the 74 verbs show their past forms, where Hindi verbs are irregular, and behind the All forms fold their present, future, subjunctive and imperative by person. Real example sentences come with 614 of the 750 words, three apiece for 427 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, gender, forms and romanisation: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
